name: Cover Letter
useWhen: Use this when you're applying for a job and need a letter to go with your resume.

sections.label: Greeting
sections.tip: Use the hiring manager's name if the job post gives it. If not, "Dear Hiring Manager:" is fine.

sections.label: The job and why you're writing
sections.what: Name the job, where you saw it, and one reason you're a strong fit.
sections.tip: Name the exact job title. Hook them with your best fact.
sections.good: I'm applying for the Office Assistant job posted on Indeed. I bring two years of front-desk experience and a 98% customer rating.
sections.bad: I want a job at your company.
phrases: I'm applying for the [job title] position posted on [site].

sections.label: Your skills (tell a STAR story)
sections.what: One short true story that proves you can do this job.
sections.tip: Pick a story that matches a skill the job post asks for.
sections.good: At Valley Hardware, I cut shipping time from 3 days to 1 by reorganizing the packing area.
sections.bad: I'm a hard worker and a team player.

sections.label: Why this company
sections.what: Why you want to work there in particular.
sections.tip: Name one real detail about the company: a product, value, or project.
sections.good: I admire how Sunrise Dental offers free cleanings to local kids every summer.

sections.label: Ask for an interview
sections.what: Ask for an interview and say how to reach you.
sections.tip: Ask directly. Give your phone or email.
sections.good: I would welcome the chance to interview. You can reach me at (661) 555-0142.
sections.bad: Hope to hear from you maybe.
phrases: I would welcome the chance to interview…
I'd love to talk about how I can help…

sections.label: Closing
sections.what: Thank them, then a formal sign-off.
sections.tip: Thank them for their time, then "Sincerely,".
sections.good:
Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
phrases: Thank you for your time and consideration.
Thank you for reviewing my application.

sections.label: Signature
sections.what: Your full name and contact info.

topics.name: General
topics.tone: Confident and specific. Prove it with a story instead of a claim.
dos: Tell one true story with a number
donts: Send the same letter to every company

topics.name: Entry-Level
topics.tone: Eager and honest. School, volunteer, and side jobs count.
dos: Use school, volunteer, or club experience
Name a skill from the job post

skills.tip: Your story can come from school, a club, volunteering, or a part-time job.
skills.good: As treasurer of my school's robotics club, I tracked a $2,000 budget and kept us under it all year.

topics.name: Career Change
topics.tone: Show how your old skills transfer to the new job.
dos: Connect your past job to this one
Show why you're making the switch

job.tip: Say what you did before and why it prepared you for this.
job.good: After six years as a restaurant manager, I'm applying for the Office Coordinator role, where my scheduling and budgeting skills fit well.

skills.tip: Pick a story from your old job that uses a skill this job needs.
